Two families: (A) TdrBuf.h binary PACK/UNPACK primitives that operate on a TdrBuf struct {base@0, pos@4/pos-word@1, length@8/len-word@2} and read/write raw positional bytes (NOT the 0x99 tagged TLV form; this is TDR 'compact'/fixed-layout binary). PACK path assert is TdrBuf.h line 0xe0/0x108/0xc4; UNPACK path assert is 0x92/0x290. (B) TdrBufUtil.cpp DebugFormat/dump functions that emit a human-readable text representation of a struct: helper FUN_1024a290(buf,indent,sep,"[name]",fmt,val)=scalar field, FUN_1024a410=string field, FUN_1024a140=open/indent, FUN_1010c010=append formatted, FUN_1024a1e0=nested-struct label, FUN_1024a3b0=array-open. Format DATs: DAT_11d9e0b4="%d"(int32), DAT_11d9f574="%u"(uint32), DAT_11d9f710=array-element fmt, DAT_11da4eb8=struct-label fmt. The DebugFormat functions are the authoritative source of full field names/offsets and array size caps; the auto-generated 0x99 TLV docs are a SUBSET (see TlvFriendRoleInfo discrepancy). None of these run server-side per se, but the server MUST reproduce identical struct layouts, field order, and honor the same array size limits when (de)serializing these payloads.
